claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially has a high-temperature, single-phase BCC structure.
The initial high-temperature BCC phase in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is metastable.
Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 has a composition-dependent thermodynamic driving force for ordering or phase separation.
The proposed thermodynamic instability arises from unfavorable mixing enthalpies involving Cr with Co, Fe, or Ni.
Sluggish atomic diffusion in this complex alloy kinetically counteracts the thermodynamic driving force for ordering.
Rapid cooling suppresses ordering by kinetically limiting atomic redistribution.
Isothermal aging at 600–700 °C will enable the formation of ordered secondary phases in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
The secondary ordered phases produced by aging will nucleate and grow as precipitates within the BCC matrix.
The precipitates formed during aging are likely to be Cr-rich.
Precipitation during aging will transform Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 from single-phase BCC to a multiphase microstructure.
Aged samples will exhibit new diffraction peaks, precipitate features, and compositional segregation relative to quenched samples.
The compositional segregation in newly formed phases will especially involve Cr enrichment.
Rapidly quenched Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 will retain a uniform, single-phase BCC microstructure.
The proposed relationship applies when diffusion is sufficiently activated in the 600–700 °C aging range.
The proposed relationship is not expected to apply at temperatures above 800 °C.
Non-isothermal or excessively high-temperature treatments may introduce complete phase separation or grain coarsening as additional mechanisms.
The critical aging temperature and duration required for detectable ordering are uncertain.
A comparison between samples from the same batch that are rapidly quenched or aged isothermally can test the hypothesis.
The absence of secondary ordered precipitates and compositional segregation after aging would falsify the proposed thermodynamic–kinetic balance.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that diffusion kinetics are the only varied parameter, but quenching versus aging changes temperature and thermal history, which can also change the thermodynamic driving force and equilibrium phase stability invoked by the mechanism.
